A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 17-page versions of the same study, including Appendices A–F. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection establish that the figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations, prediction-shift analyses, and a perturbation case study in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–F, with numerical results in Tables 1–11.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical analyses and benchmark results, including the main-text experiments and supplementary results in Tables 7–11.

M1.justification: Prompt-Based Adjustment, Output Layer Modification, and standalone application of the adaptive plausibility constraint are unchanged. The descriptions of VCD, ICD, and SID also retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same POPE coverage using COCO, AOKVQA, and GQA, alongside MME, CHAIR, NoCaps, and LLaVA-Bench. Calling MSCOCO-Random a 'subset' instead of a 'dataset' does not change the evaluated data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including VCD/SID in greedy comparisons and VCD/ICD/SID in POPE sampling comparisons. The same baseline and spurious-improvement controls remain.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, greedy versus sampling procedures, benchmark subsets, and evaluation metrics are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E4.justification: The prediction-transition analyses, perturbation case study, decoding-strategy comparisons, and constraint-alone tests are retained unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–D.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 and the empirical figures retain the same results and entries. For example, Table 1 reports VCD accuracies of 88.6% on COCO-Random and 78.0% on GQA-Adversarial in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, including the contrastive distributions, plausibility constraints, and output-modification threshold rule, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, mathematical arguments, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about output-distribution bias, sampling becoming approximately greedy, and the failure of contrastive decoding to mitigate hallucinations.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning distribution balance, sampling effects, and failed visual grounding remain unchanged, including Appendix C and Section 6. The edits in Section 4.1 preserve the original explanation and scope.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, prompts, parameter definitions, and the source-code access link are unchanged. No technical or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 45 references are unchanged. The paper retains the same positioning relative to prior contrastive decoding and hallucination research.

P1.justification: v4 adds Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo as Guangzong Si's second affiliation and numbers the affiliations. Section 4.1 receives small wording edits, including 'dataset' to 'subset' and 'prediction accuracy' to 'accuracy'; section organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation block produces small layout shifts and different paragraph breaks across pages 1–5, including shifted figure and table positions. Display contents and designs are unchanged; pages 6–17 render identically.

improvement.justification: v4 updates affiliation information and makes small wording and layout adjustments. The methods, evidence, mathematical content, interpretations, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—remain unchanged, with no meaningful effect on overall paper quality.
